take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only when access, dialect or stance really differ.
Give the synthesizer a framework, such as my decision frame, or it just averages the views into a beige summary.
After a run, have the agent write the lessons into the shared rules file. The failures are at the handoffs, so check those.

monday.move: Rerun the pilot-cohort brief with fresh data using the sources-plus-synthesizer setup, with my pricing decision frame as the spine. Ask it to flag where the sources contradict each other, and put the rules file in a place the team can reach.
monday.who: Me, then a draft to the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: If the synthesizer gives an even-handed summary with no committed diagnosis, I stop and go back to one agent with one prompt.
monday.blocker: The team has no shared place for the context and rules files, so everyone has their own copy.

misconception.why: More input and better prompts gave a beige answer. What changed the result was a framework and a rules file the whole system reads. I haven't dropped the belief that prompts matter, though.

one_line: Good on where multi-agent setups break and how to write the lesson down, but it repeats the don't-split point three times, and it leaves you holding an answer you can't verify yet.
